figure_checks.clipping: No ink touches the canvas edge. The outermost non-white pixels are x=178 (the 'moments' row label) and x=1332 (the red marker's right edge), on a 1399 px canvas, and y=16 (legend text) and y=683 (x axis title) on a 720 px canvas.
figure_checks.encoding_from_the_render: Colour encodes one thing per marker, and it is applied consistently. Grey #929292 is the median over lanes; blue #3366cc is the largest lane; red #cc0000 replaces blue for the largest lane only when it exceeds 1e-10, which happens in exactly one row. The grey horizontal segment spans median to maximum on every row where the two differ. Four rows (whole cells, conic cells, normal cells, normalization) draw a single marker and one row (stationary fluxes) draws a single marker with no grey at all; these two cases are visually identical and are the subject of finding 1. The legend does not distinguish them.

findings.summary: The grey median marker is drawn at zorder 3 and the largest-lane marker at zorder 4 with the same markersize, so wherever the median equals the maximum the median mark is painted completely over and a reader sees one dot where two values are plotted. Measured on the attached render: in whole cells, conic cells, normal cells and normalization there are zero neutral anti-aliased pixels within 14 px of the marker centre, against 18 in the control row field coefficients where the two marks are 12 px apart, so the median glyph is not faintly visible but absent. Those four rows do coincide exactly in the run's own receipts (median spread equals maximum spread: 5.684e-14, 1.137e-13, 2.842e-14 and 1.137e-13), so the visible dot does carry the median value. The cost is a reading ambiguity that the caption makes worse rather than better: the caption's only rule for a single-dot row is 'A zero median is omitted from the logarithmic axis', which is true of exactly one of the five such rows (stationary fluxes, median spread 0.0) and false of these four. A reader who applies the caption's rule concludes that four stages whose lanes all share one spread have a zero median spread, and the reader has no way on the canvas to tell 'median coincident with maximum' from 'median omitted'. Four further rows (moments, scaled jets, bell coefficients, third derivatives) are partially occluded, with 35-52 visible grey pixels against 76-95 where the marks are well separated. Not blocking because no datum is lost -- the coincident dot shows the median value and the caption does explain the genuine zero -- but the two cases should be separable, for instance by offsetting the median marker or by drawing the median as a tick on the row's segment.

findings.summary: The top row plots a different quantity from every other row, on the same axis and against the same threshold rule. 'moments (1-4 ulp)' is seeded with the spread of the perturbed moment values themselves -- the input population -- while all 16 rows below it are spreads of the fresh residual after a one-ulp injection at a stage output. The x axis is labelled 'Residual spread across 64 perturbations' and the rule is the 1e-10 residual certificate, so the top row invites comparing a moment change to a residual threshold. It is also the only row that crosses the rule (its maximum marker is red at 2.4e-10, right of the certificate at 1e-10), which means the figure's single over-certificate mark is the one mark whose x value is not a residual. The caption does say 'The first row is the original one-to-four-ulp moment population', which discloses the difference in prose, but the axis label and the threshold rule are shared and unchanged, so a reader scanning the panel still reads the red marker as a stage over the certificate. Not blocking: the caption discloses it and the row is named 'moments'.

findings.summary: The fixed limits ax.set_xlim(1e-28, 1e-9) give 19 decades of logarithmic axis for data whose comparison is concentrated in two, so most of the plot width carries no data and the stages that set the floor are squeezed together. Measured on the attached render: the axes span x=377 to x=1358, 981 px at 51.6 px per decade; 24 of the 26 marks lie between x=1091 and x=1252, that is 161 px or 16 percent of the plot width; the 12 decades from 1e-26 to 1e-14 hold exactly one row (subtraction, at x=487-502) and about 620 px of empty white; the decade from 1e-10 to 1e-9 is also empty. The figure exists to show which stage's spread sits closest to the certificate, and that comparison is confined to a band narrower than the certificate diamond would be at any readable marker size, while 60 percent of the ink budget is spent on empty axis. Not blocking: every mark remains separable and the decade ticks let a reader recover any single value, and the wide limits exist to show the subtraction row's 1e-26 floor beside the certificate. A broken or two-panel axis, or limits near 1e-27 to 1e-11, would let the 16 core stages be compared at a glance.

The caption spends its last two sentences on the production process rather than on what the reader is looking at: 'The shared checked saver accepted all text bounds and overlaps on the 1400 x 720 canvas; the producer inspected the PNG rendering. Only the SVG is published.' Two of the caption's five sentences therefore describe the tooling that made the figure, and one of the two numbers it states is slightly wrong about the delivered artifact -- the attached render is 1399x720, not 1400x720. The sentences a reader needs are the ones before them, which do their job: they name the two series, explain the red mark, and state the zero-median rule. Not blocking: the caption is not a restatement of a title, the figure has no title, and nothing here misleads a reader about the data.

item_verdicts.caption_independence: The caption is not a restatement of a title: the figure carries no title, identity is in the file name, and the caption states the encoding (grey median, blue largest, red above certificate), the zero-median omission rule, which row is the moment population, and what the comparison shows. It is accurate about the drawing except for the 1400 px canvas claim and the ambiguity finding 1 records.

No label is clipped (ink stays inside 178-1358 of 1399 and 16-683 of 720), no label overlaps another label or the data, all text is 7.8:1 on white and renders at 12-20 px, and the figure does not depict tabular data, so none of the blocking categories is met.
